newsitem.title: CHINA: China offshore oil output 4.43 mln T in Jan-March.
newsitem.headline: China offshore oil output 4.43 mln T in Jan-March.

text.p: China produced 4.43 million tonnes of offshore crude oil in the first quarter, up by 31.6 percent from a year-ago, the China National Offshore Oil Corp said in a report issued by the Xinhua news agency on Thursday.
Offshore production of natural gas reached 970 million cubic metres in the first three months of this year, up by 57 percent from a year ago, it said.
"This is a record quarterly output with average daily crude output topping 49,100 tonnes," Xinhua quoted a senior official of China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) as saying.
He said oil and gas output would increase further this year, as a group of new oil and gas fields were scheduled to begin operation offshore before the end of the year.

These projects include the Xijiang 24-1 and the Lufeng 22-1 oil fields in the South China Sea, the J block of Suizhong 36-1 oilfield and Boxi oilfield group in the Bohai Sea, as well as the Jinzhou 20-2 gas field in the Bohai Sea's Liaodong Bay.
CNOOC had entered its best period of development, with all 19 operational offshore oil and gas fields producing, the official said.
Offshore oil output this year was expected to exceed the 15 million tonnes produced in 1996, while gas output would be higher than the three billion cubic metres produced last year, he said.
